derivations.claim: Distinct monomials $U^n$ have distinct degrees. Since $f$ preserves degrees, its kernel is graded: if a finite sum maps to zero, each homogeneous summand maps to zero in the direct-sum grading of $M$. Each source homogeneous summand is one-dimensional, so the kernel is spanned by the monomials it contains. Let $S=\{n\in\mathbb Z:f(U^n)=0\}$. Nonzero kernel makes $S$ nonempty, and proper kernel makes its complement nonempty. $R$-linearity makes $S$ upward closed: $n\in S$ implies $n+1\in S$. Choose one integer $b\notin S$. No integer at most $b$ is in $S$, since otherwise upward closure would put $b$ in $S$. Thus $S$ has a least integer $N$, by the well-ordering of the nonnegative integers after translating by $b+1$. Upward closure gives $S=\{n:n\ge N\}$ and hence $\ker f=U^N R$. This also proves uniqueness of $N$. Only one witness integer was selected; no family of choices was used. [given, construct, algebra]

The quotient by this kernel has vector-space basis the classes of the monomials with exponents $n<N$. Indeed, deleting the exponents at least $N$ gives a unique finite representative, and a linear combination of the remaining monomials is in the kernel only when all coefficients vanish. Applying $f$ therefore gives the independent spanning family $e_j$ in the Statement. Multiplication by $U$ kills $e_0$ and sends $e_j$ to $e_{j-1}$ for $j\ge1$. The degree formula follows by substituting $n=N-1-j$. The map from the standard quotient tower taking the class of $U^{-j}$ to $e_j$ intertwines $U$, is a vector-space bijection and shifts its bottom degree to $a-2N+2$. [step 1.1, construct, algebra]

For a nonzero finite sum $v=\sum_{j=0}^J c_j e_j$, multiplication by $U^{J+1}$ kills every term. For any fixed $k\ge1$, the finite sum $w=\sum_{j=0}^J c_j e_{j+k}$ belongs to the same image and satisfies $U^k w=v$. Zero has these properties as well. Thus local $U$-torsion and divisibility by every power hold simultaneously. A nonzero homogeneous element is exactly one $e_j$, because the degrees in step 2.1 are distinct and the coefficient field has one nonzero element. Its degree is therefore $a-2N+2+2j$, and the least is attained precisely at $e_0$. A degree-preserving bijection preserves the set of occupied degrees, so it preserves this least degree. In particular no $U$-nontorsion element exists in this tower, even though its least occupied grading is defined. These are algebraic conclusions under the stated kernel hypotheses, without a Floer existence or invariance assertion. [step 2.1, construct, algebra] ∎
